extracted.intended_audience: research funders, journal editors, peer reviewers, university promotion committees, research users and institutional leaders
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and checklists for assessing interdisciplinary research (IDR) across proposals, outputs, careers, institutes, and national evaluation exercises; aimed at reviewers, funders, publishers and institutional decision‑makers. Provides foundational principles and many specific evaluative questions for peer review and institutional assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary research definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Interdisciplinary research (IDR) is a mode of research by teams or individuals that integrates information, data, techniques, tools, perspectives, concepts, and/or theories from two or more disciplines or bodies of specialized knowledge to advance fundamental understanding or to solve problems beyond the scope of a single discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the scope for what counts as IDR and underpins all evaluative criteria in the document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation requires IDR‑specific criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluating IDR encounters difficulties when approaches based in single disciplines are applied to it and requires fresh criteria developed within an interdisciplinary context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review processes should not simply 'bolt on' IDR criteria to disciplinary review; evaluation should assume a holistic interdisciplinary perspective from the start.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for experienced IDR reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective evaluation of IDR at individual, project and institutional levels requires the judgement of researchers who are experienced in high quality IDR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels and readers should include members with IDR experience; cross‑panel co‑option and pools of IDR experts are suggested.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDR is more than additive
rubrics_metrics.description: The research must show that it has created or synthesised new insights, knowledge, theory or practice from the elements of which it is composed — not merely parallel disciplinary contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for genuine integration where ingredients 'react' and combine; superficial parallelism is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership structure (principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a team project, the leadership structure should be inclusive, transparent of roles, and ensure equality of contributing disciplines in voice and status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leadership should facilitate interdisciplinary dialogue and bring strands together into an emergent whole; avoid over‑dominant project leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources and time (principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Material and temporal requirements of each contributing discipline must be realistically met, with sufficient time/resources planned for dialogue, co‑learning and integration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active facilitation and realistic budgeting/timetabling for integrative work is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recursive benefit (principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: It should be clear how each contributing part or discipline will benefit from the effort of integration into the whole; benefits can be transformational.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether project design allows knowledge to flow back into constituent disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary ‘hospitality’ (principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects should welcome disciplinary members and their contributions on equal terms, avoiding explicit or implicit hierarchies and encouraging mutual learning and teaching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for inclusive activities, open exchanges, and generous intellectual welcome (including for non‑academic partners).

rubrics_metrics.name: Social cohesion (principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects should demonstrate attention to building communication, mutual understanding and trust among team members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether institutional structures or networks support social cohesion; consider plans for team‑building and communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scales (principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different scales — spatial, temporal and conceptual — in a project need to be identified and related, with appropriate information flow between scales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how models and objects of study are connected across scales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and objects of study (principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: The quantitative and qualitative data and objects of study need to be identified and coherently brought together, with structures for translating between them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for plans and mechanisms for integrating diverse data types and for translation across epistemologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and development (principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects should recognise opportunities and needs for development, such as training in shared methodologies or introductions to new knowledge areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess proposed training plans for participants and students to support interdisciplinary exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness and flexibility (principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Good IDR projects must demonstrate awareness that new knowledge may generate new research questions or challenges and should contain plans for such eventualities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for contingency plans and mechanisms for adapting aims and methods as the research develops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use of ‘service’ disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: When disciplines or members serve primarily in a service role (e.g. data production), it should be a considered choice rather than an assumed hierarchy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate transparency about service roles and whether such roles make full use of contributors' potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti‑patterns to avoid in IDR
rubrics_metrics.description: Practices to avoid include generating disciplinary hierarchies, non‑convergent parallel progress, exclusive framing of questions, over‑dominant leadership, and tokenistic inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these as red flags in assessment of proposals and projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall approach: genuine collaborative development
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the proposal clearly a product of genuine collaborative development?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check evidence of joint drafting, shared framing of aims, and integrative planning rather than independent inputs stitched together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall approach: explicit added value
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the proposal articulate a clear concept of added value and how it will achieve 'more than the sum of its parts' from interdisciplinary collaboration?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for explicit statements of the anticipated integrative outcomes and their novelty/utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall approach: statement of collaboration principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the proposal contain an explicit statement about underlying principles for collaboration and/or 'ground rules' for the project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess transparency about decision‑making, credit allocation, conflict resolution and collaboration norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall approach: workable grouping of disciplines/people
rubrics_metrics.description: Is it evident that the proponents have formed a workable grouping of disciplines/people?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for complementary skills, realistic roles, and documented interactions or prior collaboration where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall approach: integrated formulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the proposal integrate aims and objectives, theory, data collection and analysis, and outputs?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess coherence across sections rather than siloed descriptions for each discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall approach: institutional support structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the host institution have structures and mechanisms appropriate for supporting interdisciplinary research?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for evidence of centres, seed funding, administrative support, neutral space and training resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall approach: disruption of inward disciplinary thinking
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the proposal take into account the need to disrupt inward disciplinary thinking?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether project design actively challenges disciplinary assumptions and promotes cross‑disciplinary reflexivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall approach: engagement with larger intellectual networks
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there evidence of location in larger intellectual networks (e.g. international collaborators) and does the project support interaction with these?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider external collaborations, partnerships and networking plans as indications of intellectual reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall approach: external funders/partners
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there other funders/partners indicative of diverse disciplinary or societal support for the project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diverse partners can signal broader relevance and resourcing support; evaluate their role and contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall approach: international partners
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there international partners suggesting that the research may have interest beyond national boundaries?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International collaboration can indicate broader applicability; assess the depth and function of such links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project development: common goal
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a common goal? Does the project have high level/broader questions of common interest across the disciplinary areas involved?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that summary and detailed narratives reflect shared purpose rather than juxtaposed aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project development: appropriate disciplinary participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Have appropriate participating disciplinary areas been included and have all disciplinary participants been included realistically rather than tokenistically?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether gaps exist and whether open calls or other mechanisms were used to explore wider possibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project development: interdisciplinary formulation of research questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the formulation of research questions suggest more than a single disciplinary perspective and show intellectual inclusivity and 'hospitality'?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for questions that require integration and are not answerable within one discipline alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project development: disciplinary equality in question development
rubrics_metrics.description: Is disciplinary equality evident in collective development of research questions, aims and objectives, and are questions situated in wider debates?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate authorship and contributions to question design and contextual framing in national/international debates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project development: objects of study shared across disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the 'objects of study' and are they the purview of all disciplinary areas represented?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure objects of study are accessible and meaningful to all contributing disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project development: traversal of diverse scales
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project traverse diverse scales of analysis successfully at each stage?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how conceptual, temporal and spatial scales are connected and managed throughout the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project development: potential for recursive disciplinary feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Do research questions have the potential for useful — possibly transformational — recursive feedback into disciplinary thinking?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for explicit mechanisms or pathways for disciplinary learning arising from integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project development: vision with flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the proposal contain a clear vision of interdisciplinary aims and objectives while retaining openness and flexibility and plans for continuity over time?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance clarity of aims with built‑in adaptability and progression planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure & leadership: track record in collaborative/IDR leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Do proponents (or some contributors) have a track record in leading collaborative and ideally interdisciplinary research, or describe how they will access best practice?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If track record is limited, look for plans to bring in experienced advisors or training in IDR leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure & leadership: appropriate intellectual leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the intellectual leadership and its disciplinary expertise appropriate to the needs of the project (not defined solely by status or access to resources)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess fit between leader expertise and integrative aims rather than prestige markers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure & leadership: workable division of intellectual and fiscal responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: What arrangements ensure divisions of intellectual and fiscal responsibilities are workable (e.g. separation between project management/fiscal accountability and intellectual leadership)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek clarity on management roles, reporting lines, and governance arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure & leadership: disciplinary equality in structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project structure demonstrate application of principles of disciplinary equality and avoidance of hierarchies (e.g. in sub‑theme leadership and resource allocation)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect allocation of resources and leadership roles for signs of equality or dominance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure & leadership: interdisciplinary workstream design
rubrics_metrics.description: Are workstreams structured in an interdisciplinary way, or do they merely constitute parallel disciplinary streams?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between genuinely integrative workstreams and parallel tasks that lack convergence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure & leadership: demographic balance of participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Has thought been given to an appropriate demographic balance (senior/junior, post‑docs, PhD studentships)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate career development provisions and inclusion of early‑career researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure & leadership: clarity of roles and benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Are roles within the project and their benefits to participants clearly explained, including transparency about service roles?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether roles enable participants to gain appropriate credit and development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure & leadership: clear responsibilities for outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Have participants’ respective responsibilities in the production of outputs been clearly laid out and are these reflective of principles of equality between disciplines?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for authorship plans, contribution statements and distribution of output tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure & leadership: negotiated credit and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there evidence that credit for work has been negotiated fairly and transparently, and is presented in a way compatible with public research data reporting instruments?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for documented agreements on authorship, contribution and reporting (e.g. Researchfish compatibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure & leadership: mechanisms to keep project on track
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the proposal include mechanisms for keeping the project on track over the whole research period?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess governance, milestones, review points and contingency processes to maintain integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication & integration: realistic time/resource for epistemological exchange
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project allocate realistic time and resources to enable the epistemological exchange necessary for collective analysis?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check budgeting for meetings, retreats, facilitation and sustained dialogic activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication & integration: facilitation of knowledge exchange
rubrics_metrics.description: How will knowledge exchange between participants be facilitated (including external partners)? Is a facilitator needed or do project leaders have sufficient time/resource to provide facilitation?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify explicit facilitation roles, mediated translation mechanisms or training to support exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication & integration: provision for training to support exchanges
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there provision for training to support interdisciplinary exchanges of knowledge (for participants or students)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for plans for workshops, shared method training, or methodological induction sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication & integration: support for social relationships and networks
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the proposal recognise the need to support social relationships and collaborative networks across disciplinary boundaries within and beyond the institution?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess planned activities for network building, stakeholder engagement and maintaining team cohesion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication & integration: wider community engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: What provision has been made for wider community engagement, if appropriate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider plans for public engagement, user communities, co‑production or stakeholder interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory & methods: interdisciplinary theoretical background
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the theoretical background interdisciplinary — showing egalitarian openness and 'hospitality' in formulation of theory and framing of questions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check literature review and theoretical framing for balanced, cross‑disciplinary engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory & methods: recognition of different scales
rubrics_metrics.description: Has the theoretical design recognised the different scales of research questions and the information flow between them?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how theory links micro/macro, temporal or spatial scales coherently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory & methods: provision for theoretical contribution beyond specialisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there provision for theoretical contribution over and above disciplinary specialisms?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for explicit aims to advance integrative theorising rather than only disciplinary theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory & methods: potential to illuminate disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there potential for the project's theoretical contributions to illuminate specific disciplinary areas as well as producing 'more than the sum of the parts'?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess pathways for cross‑fertilisation of theory back into disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory & methods: employment of integrative methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project employ integrative methods alongside those necessary for each disciplinary contribution?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for methods designed to bridge epistemologies (mixed methods, translational protocols, joint coding frameworks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory & methods: training in shared methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there provision for training in the employment of shared methods of data collection and analysis?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training plans for harmonising data collection, joint analysis workshops and method standardisation are important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data, material & analysis: recognition of diverse forms of data
rubrics_metrics.description: Have proponents recognised and encompassed diversity in forms of data/material across component disciplinary areas?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check explicit plans for handling qualitative, quantitative, archival or material data and epistemic differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data, material & analysis: effective integration of diverse data
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project design demonstrate effective ways of integrating diverse data/material and differences in scale?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess proposed analytic frameworks, translation mechanisms and integrative synthesis procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data, material & analysis: openness of non‑restricted data/material
rubrics_metrics.description: Are data/materials not restricted for ethical or commercial reasons made openly available?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate data sharing plans, repositories, and access provisions consistent with ethics and IP constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data, material & analysis: integrative analytic methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the proposed analytic methods integrative of diverse disciplinary data/materials?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for joint analytic protocols, cross‑disciplinary coding schemes or combined statistical/qualitative approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data, material & analysis: provision for collaborative analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Has effective provision been made for collaborative analysis of datasets (e.g. shared platforms, workshops)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for infrastructure and time allocation for team analysis and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outputs (proposal phase): inclusivity across disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the proposed joint outputs inclusive of all disciplinary areas and workstreams actively involved in the project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess planned outputs for representation of contributions rather than privileging one discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outputs (proposal phase): diverse forms for academic and public impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there suitably diverse forms of output to enable contributions to academic fields as well as public impact?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for articles, monographs, policy briefs, exhibitions, datasets and other non‑traditional outputs as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outputs (proposal phase): equal treatment of diverse output types
rubrics_metrics.description: Are diverse forms of output treated equally (e.g. qualitative outputs not relegated to 'background')?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether assessment and resourcing reflect equal value across methods and outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outputs (proposal phase): balance between individual and joint outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a suitable balance between individual and joint outputs that collectively reflect the interdisciplinary aims?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure career needs of individuals are respected while pursuing joint interdisciplinary publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outputs (proposal phase): plan for joint interdisciplinary outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a plan for producing joint interdisciplinary outputs?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for timelines, authorship agreements and statement of intended integrative publications/products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outputs (proposal phase): support for disciplinary outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Will support be given to outputs aimed to feed back into specific disciplinary areas?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether project supports disciplinary career progression alongside interdisciplinary aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outputs (proposal phase): accessibility across disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the plan for outputs 'hospitable' so they are accessible to a range of disciplinary areas?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check language, framing and dissemination strategies to ensure cross‑disciplinary uptake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outputs (proposal phase): non‑academic audiences inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Are some outputs appropriate for engagement of other audiences, including non‑academic readers?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for tailored summaries, policy engagement plans, or public dissemination mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timetable: sufficiency for integrative exchange
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the project timetable sufficient to support a period of integrative knowledge exchange?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether schedule allows for iterative reflection, synthesis and co‑production phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timetable: accommodation of disciplinary temporal needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Have the different temporal needs of disciplines been realistically accommodated at each stage (e.g. time for data collection/analysis)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for realistic timelines for differing research cycles and outputs (e.g. longitudinal ethnography vs lab experiments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timetable: appropriate short and long term milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Do proposed milestones for events and outputs reflect realities of supporting interdisciplinary collaboration (short and long term)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate milestone framing for integration checkpoints and delivery expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timetable: risk management and contingency planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Has consideration been given to risk management and the potential for alternative research questions and challenges to arise?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for documented contingency options and processes for adapting project aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Output assessment (content): more than sum of disciplinary inputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the output constitute 'more than the sum of' the specific disciplinary inputs?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for synthesis, new questions or integrated findings that could not have arisen from single disciplines alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Output assessment (content): interdisciplinary research questions/hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the research questions and/or hypotheses clearly a new product of interdisciplinary collaboration?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess originality of framing and whether questions demand integrative approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Output assessment (content): interdisciplinary perspective in background
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the background information indicative of an interdisciplinary perspective?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check citations, framing and literature engagement across fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Output assessment (content): balanced use of literature/materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the output draw, in a sufficiently balanced manner, on literature/material from the various disciplines involved?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine citation patterns and engagement depth across contributing disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Output assessment (methodology): theoretical synthesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Do theoretical discussions reflect interdisciplinary exchange and synthesis of knowledge?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether theory is integrated rather than a sequence of disciplinary theories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Output assessment (methodology): cross‑disciplinary data/method use
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the output draw on data/materials, methods and forms of analysis from the various disciplines involved?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for mixed method fusion, comparative analyses and integrated interpretative frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Output assessment (methodology): novelty by integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the output create novelty by integrating established knowledge within disciplines and has evaluation avoided insisting on novelty within each discipline?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge novelty in integrative terms and avoid penalising outputs for not being novel in every contributing discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Output assessment (methodology): connection across scales
rubrics_metrics.description: Have different scales and objects of study of the participating disciplines been successfully connected and/or integrated?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess successful linking of micro/macro or different conceptual scales in analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Output assessment (methodology): equal valuation of contributing disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: Has each contributing discipline been valued equally in the output?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for marginalisation of certain disciplinary perspectives in interpretation or presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Output assessment (communication): incorporation of disciplinary voices
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the output incorporate different disciplinary 'voices' and ideas and if there is a lead voice does it override or enable/support others?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate authorship voice, rhetorical dominance and whether lead voice facilitates integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Output assessment (communication): accessibility to different perspectives/audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the output accessible to different disciplinary perspectives and, where relevant, wider audiences including research user communities?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess language, explanations of methods, and inclusion of summaries or translational materials for non‑specialists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Output assessment (communication): potential to inform disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the output have potential to provide transformative feedback into specific disciplinary areas?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for clear mechanisms by which integrative findings could alter disciplinary theory or practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Output assessment (communication): attention to impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the output address issues of impact?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider both academic and societal impacts and whether the output articulates pathways to influence or application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Output assessment (communication): transparent authorship and contribution credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Is authorship and disciplinary contribution credited transparently?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage contribution statements and standardised formats (e.g. CREDIT/TaXonomy) to make credit visible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer policies: explicit recruitment/probation/promotion criteria for IDR
rubrics_metrics.description: Recruitment, probation and promotion criteria should explicitly mention the value of IDR and clarify mechanisms for its evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should codify how IDR counts in career progression to reduce disincentives for interdisciplinary work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer policies: equal evaluation of interdisciplinary and disciplinary work
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers should be assured that interdisciplinary work will be evaluated and valued equally with discipline‑based projects and outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commit to evaluation practices that do not disadvantage IDR in promotion and appraisal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer policies: recognition of Co‑I leadership and integrative roles
rubrics_metrics.description: In team‑based IDR projects, Co‑I roles supervising junior staff and integrating workstreams should carry at least as much weight as a PI role in single‑discipline projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise integrative leadership and mentorship as substantial contributions in appraisal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer policies: evaluation of leadership independent of financial allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of contribution to project leadership should be unrelated to the assignment of financial resources to each aspect of an IDR project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid equating money assigned with intellectual leadership or credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer policies: training availability at all career levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Training in IDR practice and methodology should be available at all career levels, including support for setting up IDR projects and project management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should resource workshops, mentorship and practical training opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer policies: mentoring from senior IDR academics
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentoring in career planning from senior academics with IDR experience should be available to early career researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide structured mentoring programs linking early career researchers with experienced interdisciplinary mentors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer policies: support for engagement with users/external partners
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for engagement with research users and external partners is central to developing a career in IDR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide recognition, funding and infrastructure for user engagement activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer policies: resourced centres/institutes for IDR
rubrics_metrics.description: Creating and resourcing centres and institutes supporting IDR enhances delivery of support measures and signals institutional values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether institutions invest in structural support for IDR (space, admin, seedcorn funding).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishers: adherence to IDR evaluative principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers need to adhere to the evaluative principles for IDR and make use of mechanisms to identify the added value of multi‑discipline, multi‑author outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers should adapt peer review and editorial policies to recognise integrative scholarship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishers: standard author contribution statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers should include clear statements on author contributions to multi‑authored papers in an agreed standard format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend the use of standard taxonomies like CREDIT to make contributions transparent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishers: support for genuine interdisciplinary general interest publications
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a need for 'general interest' publications that support genuine IDR rather than bundling single‑discipline outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage outlets that welcome integrative work and provide appropriate review expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishers: clear criteria about valuing IDR
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers should provide clear criteria about how they value and evaluate IDR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial policies should state how interdisciplinary submissions will be assessed and by whom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research funders: embed IDR good practice in calls
rubrics_metrics.description: Funders should embed good practice in IDR and its evaluation in relevant funding calls and communicate this clearly to applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design calls with review panels and criteria suited to integrative work and provide guidance to applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research funders: sponsor development activities for ECRs
rubrics_metrics.description: Funders should sponsor 'sandpit', mentoring and development activities for fundable early career researchers drawing on experienced IDR researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support capacity building and provide pathways to funding for emerging interdisciplinary scholars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research funders: communicate IDR practice to evaluation panels
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a need to communicate good IDR practice to evaluation panels and embed this in their structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide training, guidance notes and include IDR expertise in panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research funders: recognise additional Co‑I skills and collective leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessors should recognise additional skills required of Co‑Is in large projects and the value of collective leadership models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid undervaluing integrative management and co‑lead roles when evaluating personnel contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution assessment: cross‑cutting structural mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the institution have established cross‑cutting structural mechanisms to support interdisciplinary collaboration?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate presence of centres, inter‑faculty initiatives, seed funding and administrative support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution assessment: realistic resourcing of structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Are structural mechanisms provided with resources realistic to this purpose (academic staff time and administrative support)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether funding and time allocations match the needs of IDR activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution assessment: sufficient coordination expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Do such structures contain sufficient expertise in coordinating interdisciplinary research?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for staff with experience in facilitation, knowledge exchange and interdisciplinary programme management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution assessment: access to neutral physical space
rubrics_metrics.description: Is research located in (or does it have access to) independent/neutral physical space, or if not, how is creativity encouraged?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neutral space can encourage cross‑disciplinary interaction; if absent, evaluate alternative means to foster interdisciplinarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution assessment: supportive cultural discourses
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the institution have cultural discourses, narratives and representations supportive of involvement in IDR?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how institutional messaging, leadership statements and reward systems reflect IDR value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution assessment: seedcorn funding and support staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the institution provide seedcorn funding or support staff to enable investment of time in IDR development?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seed funding and nimble administrative support are indicators of institutional commitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution assessment: reward of interdisciplinary investment
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the institution reward researchers who invest time in interdisciplinary work (e.g. in promotion and national performance exercises)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review promotion criteria, internal awards and inclusion of IDR in institutional evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution assessment: capacity to support networked links
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the institution have capacity to support networked links with researchers in other institutions nationally and internationally?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess funding, administrative facilitation and policy for external partnerships and mobility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution assessment: partnerships with external organisations
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the institution have partnerships with external organisations to support interdisciplinary impacts beyond the academy?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for engagement with industry, government, NGOs and community partners and clear pathways for impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institute/centre performance: expertise and resourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the institute or centre bring together people with necessary expertise and experience in IDR and have sufficient time and resources to assist IDR development stages?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess staffing, time allocation, and capability to support projects from conception to impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institute/centre performance: connectivity with disciplinary units
rubrics_metrics.description: Has the institute established connectivity and communication with relevant disciplinary units and articulated added value of engagement?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for outreach, joint activities and evidence of discipline engagement and perceived benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institute/centre performance: evidence of sustained interdisciplinary dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there evidence of creation of new and sustained interdisciplinary dialogue from which novel integrated research questions have arisen?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess events, seminars, collaborations and resultant projects indicating ongoing dialogic exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institute/centre performance: mature external funding outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there mature projects including externally funded projects arising from the work of the institute or centre?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for successful grant capture, sustained programmes and translation into funded research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institute/centre performance: inclusion of external collaborators and impact pathways
rubrics_metrics.description: Have external collaborators/research users been identified and welcomed and have appropriate pathways to impact been supported?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate stakeholder engagement plans and mechanisms that connect research to use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institute/centre performance: development and training provision
rubrics_metrics.description: Has the institute facilitated or ensured that researchers in its programmes receive adequate development and training in IDR and support in leading projects and proposals?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess training offerings, mentorship, and leadership development linked to IDR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institute/centre performance: international engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Has the institute generated appropriate international engagement with its programmes?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider visiting fellows, international partnerships and collaborative events as markers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institute/centre performance: communication with funders
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the institute in communication with relevant research funders?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular engagement with funders can shape opportunities and ensure alignment with funding priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institute/centre performance: contribution to institutional strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Has the institute been given opportunity to contribute to the developing research and learning strategies of its institution?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess governance inclusion and strategic input into institutional planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: National exercises: enhance 'Environment' criteria for IDR support
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhance 'Environment' evaluation criteria to specify that internal structures and training that support IDR are valued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed institutional support for IDR in national assessment environment measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: National exercises: research into behavioural effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Continue research into rich datasets from exercises (e.g. REF) to detect behavioural effects on IDR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use evaluation data to study how national exercises influence submission behaviour and IDR practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: National exercises: ensure IDR outputs read by experienced IDR readers
rubrics_metrics.description: For cross‑referenced IDR outputs ensure evaluation by readers experienced in IDR and its integrated outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitate co‑option of IDR experts where necessary and make cross‑panel reading straightforward.

rubrics_metrics.name: National exercises: experiment with interdisciplinary panels
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiment with submission to inherently interdisciplinary panels in selected topic areas (e.g. Energy, Global Policy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trial interdisciplinary panels to provide suitable evaluative contexts for integrative research.

rubrics_metrics.name: National exercises: create pool of experienced IDR researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a pool of experienced interdisciplinary researchers to include at least one on each panel and network them into a cross‑cutting moderation panel for IDR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain an expert cohort to support consistent IDR moderation across panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: National exercises: develop IDR value within impact segment
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop the value and evaluation of IDR within the impact segment of national exercises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use impact assessment to recognise interdisciplinary contributions to societal outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: National exercises: emphasise output quality over journal metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Reinforce emphasis on output quality rather than measures of journal ranking or citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid over‑reliance on journal prestige or citation counts when valuing interdisciplinary outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: National exercises: examine international processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine corresponding processes in other countries to learn good practice for assessing IDR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparative study can inform improvements and experimental changes in national evaluation frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation: expand outlets that value IDR
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a need to expand the range of outlets for academic publication that value and recognise high quality IDR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support creation and recognition of journals, book series and other media that are receptive to integrative scholarship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation: institutional 'academic hospitality' and credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Leadership and participation in IDR need personal development and recognition of 'academic hospitality' and new standards of credit in HEIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should develop crediting practices that recognise facilitation, integration and service roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation: ensure outputs are read by IDR‑experienced peers in REF
rubrics_metrics.description: In REF and similar exercises ensure cross‑referenced IDR outputs are evaluated where possible by readers experienced in IDR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operationalise cross‑panel co‑reading and co‑opting of IDR experts to avoid disadvantaging IDR submissions.
